correctness.rationale: In cubic GP(n,2), for a 1-limited dominating D, counting cut edges yields |V\D|≤|E(D,V\D)|≤|D| hence |D|≥n. Both full shores attain n. Equality is equivalent to exactly one crossing edge incident at every vertex, i.e. perfect-matching cut vertex bipartition. The 256-state four-column shift graph has only cyclic SCCs of sizes 1,1,5,5 with deterministic internal edges, proving 2+10*1_{5|n} minimum-set colorings and 1+5*1_{5|n} unordered cuts. Independently reconstructed all 256 states and 160 valid arcs and cyclic SCCs.

evidence: Nov2 classification completely lists every perfect matching cut for all n>=5 with outer word period five, hence all equality bipartitions.
General cubic equality is known from Radić et al. and used as a premise.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Prior combined complete cut classification and general easy counting equivalence imply entire later theorem. Published cut result covers the hard structural lemma.

evidence: Given each prior binary labeling, choose 1-colored vertices as D. Every vertex has exactly one opposite-colored neighbor, giving a 1-limited dominating D of size n by matching; conversely every minimum D corresponds to a prior labeling.
Earlier two 5-cycles and two loops yield exactly same multiplicities as the 256-state proof.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The old theorem plus elementary double-counting entails every new sentence (except an equivalent mask notation). The direction is rigorous, not analogy to general matching theory.

evidence: For a cubic graph with 2n vertices, a size-n 1-limited dominating set has exactly one cut edge at each vertex, hence gives perfect matching cut.
